prompt: Which comparison correctly separates Roman’s planned microlensing survey from Kepler’s transit method?
options: Both require a planet to block its own host star at regular intervals.
Microlensing always gives a resolved photograph of the planet’s surface.
A transit is caused by gravity brightening an unrelated background star.
Microlensing uses gravitational magnification of background light, whereas a transit dims the host star when a planet crosses it.
explanation: Gravitational microlensing and transits have different geometries and selection effects. Roman’s survey can complement transit discoveries with planets at wider separations or free-floating objects. A brief lensing event is generally harder to repeat and does not by itself characterize an atmosphere.
